sources.title: Linux man-pages 6.18 IPC primary-source research packet

claims.text: The candidate groups common Unix/Linux IPC by communication model: pipe/FIFO for byte channels, message queues for explicit messages, shared memory for shared state, semaphores for synchronization, UNIX-domain sockets for local client/server communication, and signals for asynchronous control notifications.

Anonymous pipes naturally fit related processes through file-descriptor inheritance while FIFOs add a filesystem rendezvous name; both are bounded unidirectional pipe channels, whereas POSIX/System V message queues exchange explicit message units and have queue/resource limits.

Shared memory exposes the same shared region to multiple processes and can reduce separate payload-transfer work, but correct access needs an explicit synchronization protocol; semaphores are coordination primitives rather than ordinary bulk payload transport.

UNIX-domain sockets support efficient local stream/datagram/seqpacket client-server IPC, while signals are asynchronous notification/control mechanisms. The candidate selects among IPC models by message semantics, topology, data size, synchronization complexity and lifecycle instead of claiming a universal fastest mechanism.
